prompt: Summarize the excerpt from 'dmoi3-tablet' (chunk 25.3) about mathematics: We need to quantify the variable. Although there are many types of quantifiers in English (e.g., many, few, most, etc.)
true_answer: We need to quantify the variable. Although there are many types of quantifiers in English (e.g., many, few, most, etc.) in mathematics we, for the most part, stick to two: existential and universal. Universal and Existential Quantifiers. The existential quantifier is ∃ and is read “there exists” or “there is.” For example, ∃ x ( x < 0 ) asserts that there is a number less than 0. The universal quantifier is ∀ and is read “for all” or “every.” For example, ∀ x ( x ≥ 0 ) asserts that every number is greater than or equal to 0.
